headline: Discussed outstanding audits, the CLA financial assessment, and projected school budget overages; approved prior minutes.
summary: The meeting covered the CLA financial operations review, the former auditor Clairmount, and the Board of Education's projected overages of about $1 million. Members also discussed a planned Legislative Council Audit Committee meeting and a proposed budget working group. The only recorded vote approved the previous meeting's minutes, 4 yes and 0 no.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the prior meeting by a 4-0 roll call vote.

plain_text:
TOWN OF HAMDEN, CONNECTICUT 
 
Finance Commission Minutes         
         
Regular Meeting 
 
6:00 PM, October 1, 2026 
  
 
Memorial Town Hall 
2372 Whitney Avenue 
Hamden, CT  06518 
 Click to View Agenda   
  
1. CALL OF THE MEETING AND TAKING OF THE ROLL   
 The meeting was called to order by Chair Commissioner R. Scolnic at 6:02 PM. 
 
The Clerk called the roll, and the following members were: 
 
Present: 
 
Commissioner Rabbi Benjamin Scolnic, Chair 
Commissioner Michael Martin 
Commissioner Arnold Margolis 
Commissioner Thomas Fortuna 
 
Absent: 
Commissioner Myles Carter-Solomon, Youth 
Commissioner Bethany McCluster 
 
Also in attendance were Director of Finance Myron Hul and Dr. Mario Ciccarini, Hamden 
Board of Education Member; Briana J. Belton-Robinson, Boards and Commissions Clerk; 
and 5 members of the public joining in person and 4 members of the public joining virtually. 
2. APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MEETING MINUTES   
 Chairman R. Scolnic requested a motion to adopt the minutes from Thursday, September 
6th, 2026. 
 
The motion was made by A. Margolis and seconded by Commissioner M. Martin. 
 
Vote by Roll Call: 
 
Yes 
Commissioner R. Scolnic  
Commissioner A. Margolis 
Commissioner M. Martin 
Commissioner T. Fortuna 
 
No 
 
Absent
Commissioner B. McCluster 
Commissioner M. Carter-Solomon, Youth 
 
The motion passed. 
 
• Roll Call Vote Summary: Yes 4, No 0, Abstentions 0, Absent 2 
 
3. PUBLIC INPUT SESSION   
 Kathy Mulo, District 7, asked about the Town’s current dealings with Clairmount, the former 
auditor, including whether communications with the Finance Department and Hamden 
Board of Education were occurring primarily by telephone rather than through meetings in 
Hamden. She also raised concerns regarding the Legislative Council’s understanding of 
the Town’s financial situation. 
 
Chris Sherk, District 2, referenced comments made by Mr. Morton and expressed concern 
that the Town was approaching three overdue audits. He referenced discussion at the 
June meeting regarding a fund balance of approximately $40 million and questioned 
whether the Town would have sufficient financial resources to complete future capital 
projects. 
 
Chris expressed concern regarding the Town’s overall financial condition and the level of 
assistance being provided by the State of Connecticut and the Municipal Finance Advisory 
Commission (MFAC). He advocated for greater outside assistance and requested 
consideration of a three-year financial plan to address the Town’s financial condition. He 
also questioned whether the Administration was adequately reviewing the Town’s finances 
and budgets and expressed concern that the Town may ultimately need to replenish its 
fund balance. 
Chris encouraged the Finance Commission and Finance Director Myron Hul to pursue 
additional assistance from the State. 
 
Elaina Sherk, District 2, echoed the concerns expressed by Chris. 
 
Commissioner T. Fortuna asked about the CLA audit. Chairman R. Scolnic stated that the 
CLA matter would be discussed later under the Regular Agenda. 
4. REPORT FROM EX-OFFICIO MEMBERS   
 
 
  1. Public Official or municipal employee representing the Mayor, designated by the  
Mayor  
  No report was provided by a representative designated by the Mayor. 
  2. Representative of the Board of Education, designated by a majority vote of said 
Board  
  The Board of Education representative reported that the BOE had held its first 
Finance Subcommittee meeting and was currently projecting approximately $1 million 
in budgetary overages. 
 
Approximately 145 students with Individualized Education Programs (IEPs) entered
the Hamden school district for the 2026–2027 school year. The students are entitled 
to appropriate educational services under law. It was reported that some out-of-district 
placements, including transportation and related services, can result in six-figure 
costs. 
 
The BOE will review other areas of its budget to determine whether reductions can be 
made to offset these additional expenditures. 
 
The representative explained that an outplacement may occur when a student is 
identified as requiring services beyond those that can be provided within the school 
system. Such placements involve agreement among the school district, the student's 
parents or guardians, and the receiving educational program. It was noted that the 
addition of 145 students with IEPs represents a significant consideration for a highly 
mobile school district. 
Discussion followed regarding state education funding. The BOE plans to participate 
in a legislative forum at Cross High School to discuss cost-sharing and disparities in 
education funding among Connecticut municipalities. 
 
The BOE and its Special Education Department have also requested an external 
audit/review of special education services being provided by the district. The 
anticipated cost was reported to be approximately $60,000 to $100,000. Concerns 
were expressed regarding the services currently being provided and opportunities to 
evaluate their effectiveness and associated costs. 
 
Commissioner T. Fortuna discussed comparative per-student expenditures among 
school districts, noting that some districts spend approximately $60,000 per student, 
compared with approximately $30,000 per student in Hamden and approximately 
$20,000 per student in New Haven. 
 
The BOE representative discussed the importance of communication among the 
Board of Education, Legislative Council, Mayor’s Office, and Finance Department. 
The BOE emphasized its intention to communicate emerging budget pressures as 
they occur rather than waiting until the conclusion of the fiscal year and subsequently 
facing criticism for expenditures that could not have been anticipated. 
Commissioner T. Fortuna asked Director M. Hul whether the Finance Department 
maintains a similar level of communication and transparency with the Legislative 
Council and Mayor’s Office. 
  3. Chair of the Legislative Council committee of jurisdiction over the budget or a 
member  
of said committee designated by the Chair  
  Legislative Council member S. Gallagher reported that the Council’s Audit Committee 
meeting is scheduled for October 8, 2026, at 6:00 pm. The meeting is open to the 
public (https://zoom.us/j/96032210583). 
 
The Audit Committee’s initial objectives will include reviewing the Finance Department 
organizational chart and receiving an update regarding the outstanding audits. 
 
Chairman R. Scolnic questioned why an Audit Committee had only recently been 
reestablished and had not remained in place, noting the financial oversight
responsibilities of the Legislative Council and its Finance Committee. 
 
The Commission asked whether Finance Commissioners could attend the Audit 
Committee meeting. 
 
Council Member S. Gallagher said an Audit Committee existed when she first joined 
the Legislative Council. Council Member S. Gallagher further reported that the 
Legislative Council plans to develop a schedule or process to improve communication 
between the Finance Department and the Legislative Council. 
 
Discussion followed regarding the Legislative Council’s available recourse if required 
audits are not completed by the Administration. Gallagher stated that the CLA review 
should help identify deficiencies and determine what is needed so the Commission 
can develop a plan moving forward. 
 
The Commission also discussed whether the Legislative Council would authorize 
funding for additional personnel or other resources needed to address identified gaps. 
 
During discussion of the Legislative Council’s responsibilities, Gallagher objected to 
placing responsibility for the entire Legislative Council solely upon her. Chairman R. 
Scolnic stated that he stood by his previous comments. 
 
Director M. Hul stated that he was aware of Legislative Council communications and 
participation in discussions involving CBIZ, Clairmount, and CLA concerning 
completion of the Town’s outstanding audit work. 
 
Chairman R. Scolnic stated that he believed the Mayor was working with the State of 
Connecticut on the Town’s financial and budgetary issues. He noted that, as he 
understood it, additional steps would be required before the State could intervene 
more extensively or impose financial oversight. 
5. UPDATE REPORT FROM THE FINANCE COMMISSION CHAIR   
 Chairman R. Scolnic said he believes the Mayor is working with the State of Connecticut 
on the Town’s finances and budget. Chairman R. Scolnic noted that, based on his 
understanding of the process, additional steps may be required before the State would 
undertake a more extensive intervention or assume greater financial oversight of the Town. 
 
  
6. UPDATE REPORT FROM THE MUNICIPAL BOARD AND COMMISSIONS, INVITED 
GUEST   
 No additional reports were presented. 
7. EXECUTIVE SESSION 
(if recommended by the town attorney)  
 No Executive Session was held. 
8. REGULAR AGENDA   
 
 
 1.  Review of CLA Financial Operations Organizational Assessment
Commissioner T. Fortuna noted that the CLA contract contemplated an approximately 
six-week process. 
 
Director M. Hul stated that the overall process was expected to take approximately 10 
to 12 weeks to produce results. He further reported that a separate group would be 
reviewing tax collection operations, including labor, contracts, organizational charts, 
and related matters. Requested information had been provided several weeks earlier, 
and the kickoff was scheduled for November 13, 2026. 
 
Commissioner T. Fortuna asked whether Finance Commissioners and other key 
outside stakeholders should be permitted to participate in the kickoff meeting. He 
noted that the contract contemplated the involvement of key stakeholders prior to the 
kickoff and discussed his understanding of how the assessment process should 
proceed. 
 
Director M. Hul stated that CLA would begin with interviews. 
 
Director M. Hul confirmed that the assessment would include the Town’s computer 
software systems, tax roll, payroll, and related processes. He acknowledged that the 
Town currently relies on numerous manual processes, including pen-and-paper 
procedures, that could benefit from automation to reduce inefficiencies and errors. 
 
Commissioner T. Fortuna raised concerns regarding the extent to which Legislative 
Councils have historically been briefed and engaged on financial and budgetary 
matters. 
 
Director M. Hul stated that the level of financial knowledge and engagement among 
Legislative Council members has varied over the years. Some Council sessions 
developed expertise in municipal finance and were highly engaged in financial and 
budget matters, while other sessions were less engaged. He recalled instances in 
which individual Council members indicated that they had not campaigned on 
finances or the budget and therefore did not intend to vote on those matters. 
 2. Information Item RE Former Auditor 
       
  Chairman R. Scolnic asked whether the Town requested that Clairmount, the former 
auditor, help resolve outstanding audit-related matters. 
 
Director M. Hul stated that the Town had requested assistance. He explained that the 
Finance Department could not locate certain Town financial records from 2023. 
 
Commissioner A. Margolis asked how long the Town is required to retain such 
documents. 
 
Director M. Hul stated that Clairmount had provided the documents requested from 
the firm; however, the Finance Department had been unable to locate certain internal 
Town records, including items such as bank reconciliations. 
Discussion continued regarding the availability of documentation needed to complete 
the Town’s outstanding audit work.
3. Creation of a Commission work group 
 
The Hamden Finance Commission, whose authority is prescribed in the Hamden Town 
Charter, is forming a work group (of no more than two commissioners) to provide the 
Full Commission with details on the Town's fiscal policy matters. 
 
The Budget Working Group will gather information and report to the Full Commission 
on matters including but not limited to: 
 
• Budget Preparation and Oversight 
• Financial Reporting  
• Collective Bargaining Agreements 
• Pensions 
• Long-term Financial and Capital Planning 
• Standards and Policies 
• Best Practices and Standard 
 
       
  The agenda called for consideration of creating a Finance Commission work group 
consisting of no more than two Commissioners to gather information and report to the 
full Commission regarding Town fiscal policy matters. 
 
The proposed Budget Working Group’s areas of review include budget preparation 
and oversight, financial reporting, collective bargaining agreements, pensions, long-
term financial and capital planning, standards and policies, and municipal financial 
best practices. 
9. UNFINISHED BUSINESS   
 No unfinished business was discussed. 
10. NEW BUSINESS   
 No new business was discussed. 
11. ADJOURNMENT   
 
A motion was made to adjourn the meeting by Commissioner A. Margolis and seconded by 
Commissioner T. Fortuna. 
The motion passed unanimously. 
The Finance Commission meeting was adjourned at approximately 7:15 PM.
